CANONICAL_NAME.value: buddy_alloc -- a header-only buddy memory allocator (Stanislav Paskalev)

VERSION.value: github.com/spaskalev/buddy_alloc master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)

value.lineage: Buddy allocation (Knowlton 1965, Knuth): split memory into power-of-two blocks, merge free 'buddies' on release; the allocator behind many kernels' page allocators, trading internal fragmentation for O(log n) alloc/free and fast coalescing

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: fixed-arena allocation with fast coalescing (the buddy system)

value.built_to: allocate and free memory from a FIXED arena in power-of-two blocks, merging freed buddies so large blocks become available again -- fast coalescing under a hard capacity bound
value.pressure: a fixed, bounded arena (no asking the OS for more) where fragmentation must be fought or large requests fail while small free blocks litter the arena
value.success_means: requests satisfied while any contiguous block of the size exists, with bounded internal fragmentation and O(log n) operations

value.pressure: a fixed memory arena, fragmentation, mixed allocation sizes
value.failure_condition: fragmentation defeats it: a large request fails though enough total memory is free (just not contiguous); the kernel/embedded system runs out of usable memory

ANCESTRY.value: Buddy allocation (Knowlton 1965, Knuth): split memory into power-of-two blocks, merge free 'buddies' on release; the allocator behind many kernels' page allocators, trading internal fragmentation for O(log n) alloc/free and fast coalescing
